verdict.rationale: OpenClaw describes itself as a gateway to 'AI coding agents' and ships an `exec` tool that runs mutating shell commands in the workspace (create, edit, delete files), so cloning, editing and running tests through the shell is in scope. The release notes cite 'repository-backed cloud work', and community commenters say it embedded Claude Code as its harness via `claude -p` (the documented 'Claude CLI as the message provider' option). Sub-agents and Swarm add orchestration of parallel work. Missing for 10: first-party docs describing how it supervises external coding agents (Claude Code/Codex) end to end, explicit clone/test workflow documentation, and hands-on corroboration of repo work done by an embedded coding agent.
